brief.headline: Push for a 16.6% cut on the 100 ml PET bottle to match our best price of ₹1.87/NOS, and tighten payment to 15 days in exchange for roughly 10% off.

priceAsk.summary: Cut the 100 ml amber PET bottle price by 16.6% to ₹1.87/NOS, matching what Suraj Blow Plast gives us.
priceAsk.target: ₹1.87/NOS on PET BOT AMBER 100ML/25MM NECK 12.5G (from current ₹2.18/NOS), saving ₹28644 annually.
priceAsk.basis: We already pay ₹1.87/NOS to Suraj Blow Plast for the same bottle — TPAC is 16.6% higher with no quality or service reason for the gap. The market verdict on similar caps (₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, headroom to ₹0.65–0.80) shows rigid plastic packaging has room to move at higher volume.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days after receipt to 15 days — offer a price cut of roughly 10% in return (close to their borrowing cost of 10.27%).
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹46539 in cash for us; in exchange, offer them a discount roughly matching what they pay to borrow money (10.27%), so earlier payment is worth more to them than the rate cut costs.

brief.financialLeverage: TPAC is solid — they earn ₹637.48 Cr in revenue, keep about ₹4 of every ₹100 they sell (3.8% net), and carry an [ICRA] A / Stable credit rating with low debt (0.19x debt-to-equity). But their cash is stuck for 79 days (same as peer median 79d), and they pay suppliers in just 17 days while waiting 67 days to collect — so cash is tighter than the rating suggests. We're tiny to them (0.02% of revenue, ₹11.32 L spend), which means alone we have almost no pull. However, they borrow money at about 10.27%, so faster payment is real money to them, and the grey-zone distress signal (Altman Z 2.77) plus GST and EPF filing delays hint at some strain. Bundle our ask with a multi-year commitment or bring in one of the strong alternates to create competition — then we have enough weight to close the 16.6% price gap and shorten terms.

evidence.point: TPAC charges us ₹2.18/NOS for the 100 ml PET bottle, 16.6% above our best price
Closing that gap saves us ₹28644 a year
TPAC's cash is tied up for 79 days, matching the peer median, but they pay suppliers in only 17 days while collecting in 67 days
They borrow at an effective rate of 10.27%, so early payment is worth that much to them
We spend ₹11.32 L, just 0.02% of their ₹637.48 Cr revenue — we're a very small customer
Their Altman Z score of 2.77 puts them in the grey zone, and they have GST and EPF filing delays
evidence.figure: altmanZ: 2.77, zone: grey, riskFlags: GST filing delays, EPF payment delays

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B (65/100), and a proven pharma specialist for bottles, caps and preforms — the strongest second-source candidate to bring into an RFQ.

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd
alternates.why: Listed PET bottle and jar specialist (Pearlpet brand) — a direct fit for our 100 ml PET bottle and a credible alternate to benchmark TPAC's price.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader serving pharma with pails, containers, bottles and closures — strong and profitable, a robust second source for our packaging needs.

risks: At 0.02% of their revenue we have almost no leverage on our own — if we push hard without bundling more volume or running a competitive RFQ with Manjushree or Pearl, TPAC can easily walk away.

The grey-zone distress signal (2.77 Altman Z) and the GST/EPF delays suggest some operational strain — squeeze too hard and a fragile supplier might stumble, leaving us scrambling for qualified alternates mid-year.

TPAC pays suppliers in 17 days but collects in 67 days, so their cash is tight despite the A rating — if we push for 15-day payment without offering a meaningful rate cut (near their 10.27% borrowing cost), they'll say no and we gain nothing.

The market backup leads (Reliance, Srichakra, IVL Dhunseri, etc.) are manufacturers or recyclers, not yet qualified or priced — treat them as long-term sourcing homework, not ready alternates for this negotiation.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to talk about bringing your 100 ml PET bottle price in line with our best supplier at ₹1.87 — and in return, we can move to 15-day payment, which at your borrowing rate of 10.27% puts real money back in your pocket.
